subject.title: [Feature]: Support plugin-requestable session isolation for trust boundaries

question: Should OpenClaw expose plugin-requestable quarantined execution as a public Plugin SDK/runtime contract, and what isolation and trust-metadata guarantees must it make?
rationale: The missing capability is real, but it defines a security boundary and public plugin contract; automation cannot safely choose the enforcement semantics, result metadata shape, or prerequisite hook dependencies.

options.title: Keep As Design Item
options.body: Keep this open until maintainers define isolation semantics, prerequisite hook context, trust metadata, compatibility expectations, and validation requirements.

options.title: Document Current Primitives Only
options.body: Document sessions_spawn with sandbox=require, per-agent tool policy, audit, and separate gateway/OS boundaries as the supported workaround without adding a hook directive yet.

options.title: Reject Hook-Level Quarantine
options.body: Close the direction if maintainers decide strong isolation must remain an operator-managed gateway, OS-user, host, or sandbox deployment boundary only.

recommendation.title: Keep As Design Item
recommendation.body: Keep this open until maintainers define isolation semantics, prerequisite hook context, trust metadata, compatibility expectations, and validation requirements.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history on subagent/session runtime and security-sensitive plugin approval surfaces that this contract would extend.
